text:

I want to express my gratitude to Union Pacific Railroad for the opportunity they've provided. Serving for over a year with this amazing company has been an enriching experience. Despite the recent whirlwind of management reorganization, I understand that UP needs to make tough decisions to advance its vision. I am filled with nothing but #gratitude towards Union Pacific, as they have supported me to the best of their ability, introduced me to some amazing people who will become lifelong friends, and have not left me in a difficult situation.

When I left Dallas last year for this opportunity, leaving behind many friends and multiple job offers, many asked why I would move to Omaha. My answer has always been driven by my passion for transportation: "I like to swim against the current 🙂" #Omaha has been both beautiful and kind to me. I'm excited to announce that I'm going to become a first-time dad around April 2024, a #blessing my wife and I will cherish for years to come. I'm thankful to my wife, Iyswarya, for staying strong through this interesting situation. So, Union Pacific will be remembered fondly.

I know that some have been affected by these workforce adjustments. To those who might need a bit of extra support or someone to bounce ideas off, I'm here to chat. Tough times create strong people. Feel free to reach out.

Once again, thank you so much Union Pacific! My best wishes to "Build America" strong. And remember, it's a small world – we may bump into each other again in the future. Happy thanks giving! 🙏

A few weeks ago, I had the opportunity of being a panel member and guest speaker at an AI/ML summit. During the event, I was posed with a thought-provoking multi-layered question about the quest and curiosity surrounding the data culture from a moderator from Stanford's business. Specifically, we explored the approach to building a data culture: Is it top-down or bottom-up?

I wanted to take a moment to share my viewpoint with all of you through this short video. Watch as I delve into the topic, sharing my insights and perspectives on nurturing a thriving data culture within organizations, I emphasized the significance of upskilling and reskilling in today's rapidly evolving data landscape. By continuously developing our skills, we can adapt to the changing demands of the industry. Did you know that by 2030, it's estimated that 1.2 billion individuals globally will need reskilling and upskilling to meet the demands of the future in the data and AI/ML space? 🌍📈

I firmly believe that a successful data culture is a result of both top-down leadership and bottom-up enthusiasm. It's about fostering a collaborative environment where everyone values and embraces data-driven practices.

I invite you all to watch the short video and share your thoughts in the comments below on what you think

note: Women's Month, Avni and the NICU
text:
Happy #Women's Month! Last year, I shared my story about my last name, Veeramani, which is my mom's name, during Women's Month. This year, I have another lady joining my life, Avni Balaji Iyswarya, my daughter. Yes, she got her mom's name as her last name too.

While we were going through the whirlwind of changes at Union Pacific last November (I always believed it happened for a reason), we found out that Iyswarya was dilated on November 22nd during our regular 5-month ultrasound checkup. We were happy seeing the gender reveal of our baby while everything seemed to be going well. However, our happiness was shattered by non-symptomatic dilation. The doctors confirmed the 1 cm dilation, and they said we were lucky to diagnose the dilation upfront. The high-risk pregnancy doctors said, "If it had been delayed by another 4 days, we would have seen the baby while Iyswarya was watching TV." Initially, we had scheduled the 5-month checkup for December 5th, 2023, but due to the Union Pacific Railroad job situation, I preponed the checkup to stay intact with the insurance (that's why everything happened for a reason). Iyswarya underwent cervical stitches to hold the baby for some more time.

From that point on, Iyswarya and I took one day at a time and pushed every week with the high-risk pregnancy. I made decisions around the baby, and nothing deviated me. We pushed until the 34th week, and we planned for a small baby shower on March 8th, but our daughter came on March 4th after 19 hours of labor. Another strong woman, Iyswarya's mom, came all the way from India. She had never traveled to the USA and went through visa hassles to support her daughter and granddaughter. #Thanks to USCIS for showing humanity by providing the emergency visa slot for my mom and mother-in-law, even though the wait time for a regular visa was 400 days.

Despite all the hassles, we have Avni, who came early and spent 3 weeks in the NICU, fighting her way back home. This whole story is very personal but has a lot of learnings. As I shared last year, women are natural nurturers, and with my daughter, I also feel they are natural healers. Doctors recommended giving skin-to-skin time for Avni for her brain development. Whenever I put her on my chest for skin-to-skin time, I always felt healed by her. It has been a long journey, but it was totally worth it. We have faced immense hardships from the outset, but it also gave Iyswarya and me the opportunity to handle tough situations as gracefully as we can.

Women are unbelievable nurturers and healers. I'm lucky to have my first baby as a girl. We are committed to nurturing her fighting spirit as a future leader who can heal many in her own way.
Let's celebrate the special women in our life!

note: Testing Bard on his own talk
text:
In early 2023, as a guest speaker at an AI/ML summit, I discussed AI's capacity to think outside the box, emphasizing the potential for growth in the field. At that time, while #chatgpt was gaining attention, Bard was less known. As an AI enthusiast, I tested both, noting ChatGPT's superior conversational capabilities compared to Bard.

Recently, I had Bard analyze a video of mine discussing AI advancements, but it misinterpreted my views, suggesting GPT was less advanced than it. As I mentioned in my video, we have evolved significantly, and this incident underscores Bard's rapid progress, which is impressive. However, it also raises concerns about its biased analysis, claiming Bard is better than GPT, which directly contradicts what I said in my interview. It's a reminder of the challenges in AI development, especially in achieving unbiased interpretations. Such issues could arise with any models if proper guardrails are not in place.

Here is what Bard has to say today on my video. Please watch the short video and read through Bard's analysis of it below and evidence the bias 🙂.

note: Women's Day, his mother · 157 reactions, 11 comments (best shown)
text:
Happy International Women's Day!

On this special day, I want to express my #gratitude to all the women in my life who have played a vital role in making my life beautiful.

I would like to share my personal story and pay tribute to my heroine, my mom Veeramani. Despite getting married at the age of 14 in an arranged marriage(Yes! She was a kid), she went on to become a mother at 15 and again at 19. She faced numerous hardships and sleepless nights to ensure that my younger brother and I had the best possible life. She was a young girl herself, raising two children, but her persistence and unwavering dedication towards education ensured that my brother and I are the first-generation graduates in our family today. Her vision and commitment to education and values are what led us to where we are today. That's the reason why I carry her in my last name as my identity (Yes, Veeramani is my mom's name)

I believe that every story about women is special, and there are countless inspiring stories out there. Women are natural nurturers, and I would like to take this opportunity to express my gratitude to all the special human beings who have made a difference in their own unique ways.

In 2008, my mentor and guru in NLP - Ashok Subramanian introduced me to the world of Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP), and I am forever grateful for the impact he has had on my personal and professional growth.

As I reflect on 15 years of knowing NLP, I want to express my deepest appreciation and gratitude to Ashok for being more than a mentor to me. He has been a source of inspiration, motivation, and guidance throughout my journey. Thanks to his mentorship, I have become a certified diplomat(2010) and a practitioner(2012) in NLP, and it has been critical to my professional and personal journey.

Thank you, Ashok Subramanian for everything you have done for me. I feel privileged to have had you in my life and will always cherish the memories and lessons learned during our time together in the workshops.

note: St. Louis road trip, transport museum · 88 reactions, 2 comments
text:
Last weekend, my wife and I went on a road trip to St. Louis to attend a show by her favorite Indian comedian. Unfortunately, I couldn't get tickets to the Dallas show, so we took a seven-hour drive from Omaha to attend the St. Louis show instead.

During our stay, we had a minor accident on Sunday and it led us to take a day off on Monday and explore the area. We found a transport museum nearby, and as a kid, I was always fascinated by transportation due to my father's transport business (he had a trucking company called Balajee Transport) back in India. My dad had around 50 to 55 employees, and he made a considerable fortune from it before losing everything, so I was told to pursue any career except the transport business and eventually I got into IT :) #destiny

At the museum, I learned more about the transportation history of the United States and the significant role that the Union Pacific Railroad (UPRR) played in it for over 160 years. While there, I met Doug, who worked as an engineer and conductor at the museum. Though he wasn't working for UPRR, he had immense respect for the company and its contribution to American history.

Doug and I connected instantly, and we bonded over our shared passion for transportation. Our conversation gave me more insight about the train on display and how UPRR is shaping the future of transportation in the United States. As someone who's been with UPRR for six months now, I'm proud to be part of a team that has such a rich history and I'm excited to be part of the team shaping the future of transportation through our work in the technology division of UPRR.

This unexpected detour taught me once again to #appreciate life's surprises and the importance of following our passions. It also reminded me that even when things don't go according to plan, they can lead to unexpected discoveries and meaningful connections.

I want to extend my heartfelt thanks to the Union Pacific LEAD Lead. Educate. Achieve. Develop. team for putting together an absolutely fantastic conference! #BeBOLDandLEAD

Being a part of the organizing committee was an absolute joy, and I feel incredibly humbled to have been honored with the Develop Award, which I proudly accepted on behalf of all the hardworking members of our incredible LEAD committee. Thank you Katie Novak April Podraza for roping me in.

I also want to express my gratitude to my fellow LEAD committee members for their support. They not only allowed me to introduce the theme song I created for the conference utilizing AI capabilities, but also entrusted me with producing videos featuring our Union Pacific leaders, who shared valuable insights. Their encouragement and the opportunity to showcase these materials during the event were highly valued.

I want to give special thanks to our Union Pacific leaders Jennifer Hamann Eric Gehringer Kenny Rocker Jeremy Givens for taking the time to collaborate with me during the filming process and for generously sharing their insights. Your involvement added substantial value, and we truly appreciate it.

Congratulations Lance Fritz on your well-deserved retirement after 23 years of dedicated service as Union Pacific Railroad CEO. Your leadership, marked by humility and strength, has been truly inspiring. Our brief interactions showcased your genuine dedication to the company, culture and its employees. Your legacy will undoubtedly continue to guide and motivate countless individuals in their leadership journeys.

Best wishes for this new chapter in your life!
